entities.name: Adeodatus I
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pope Adeodatus I (reigned 615–618), also known as Deusdedit, was the first pope of Roman birth in many decades — a distinction that reflected the increasing non-Roman and non-Italian origins of the papacy in the preceding generations. His pontificate was brief but came at a critical moment in the history of the Roman Church, between the pontificates of Gregory the Great (590–604) and those of his successors who navigated the early decades of Byzantine imperial pressure, Lombard military threat, and the emerging autonomy of the Roman Church.

Deusdedit is notable for his care of the clergy and the poor. Unlike his immediate predecessors who had been monks, Deusdedit was a secular priest — a Roman by birth and formation — and this gave his pontificate a different character from the monastic papacies that surrounded it. He reportedly showed exceptional care for plague victims in Rome during an outbreak that marked his brief reign.

His canonisation as a saint reflects the early medieval Church's recognition of the pastoral holiness of bishops and popes who served faithfully under difficult conditions. His feast day is 8 November. His pontificate represented a moment of continuity for the Roman Church between the transformative papacy of Gregory I and the turbulent decades that followed as the Church and the Byzantine Empire negotiated their increasingly separate trajectories.
